resolved_findings.evidence: Module documentation and maintainer guide now require Python3.11.4+ with data-filter support. require_python checks version, tomllib, extractall filter parameter and callable data_filter before parsing/dispatch; generate and export_source also call the guard. Existing test and independent representative-API probes reject3.11.0,3.11.3, old extractall signature, absent data_filter and absent tomllib with TEMPLATE.PYTHON_UNSUPPORTED; generate is never called. Current3.11.9 artifact suite passes.

Both script suite workflow contexts now install jsonschema>=4.18,<5 using the same interpreter used by their tests. Independent fresh-environment full suite and real pinned smoke pass without schema mocking or validation skips. Shared prerequisite cherry-pick7f183d5 identifies source4d27523d2919b8e0c0e6d0f9287c5e4fc9736e56 and preserves the same six added workflow lines; sprint records sole c1 authorship. This resolves the observed missing dependency mechanism. Current-head hosted CI remains a separate merge gate.

TemplateError now supplies stable TEMPLATE-prefixed code, message, cause object and concrete recovery text through as_dict(). main emits a single stdout JSON envelope for both success and caught failure, including parser usage errors, and preserves the documented conventional --help path. run() preserves command, cwd, exit_status, stdout and stderr in UPSTREAM_FAILED and UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT causes; deadlines are included for timeout recovery. Specific codes distinguish pin mismatch, invalid answers/mapping/destination/baseline, tool availability/version and I/O failures. The maintainer procedure documents envelope fields, stdout/stderr and exit behavior, upstream diagnostic fields and stable code recovery table. ErrorContractTest checks actual CLI envelopes, empty stderr, usage/destination/mapping/missing-file errors, real schema validation and preserved upstream cause; GenerationTest checks real child stdout/stderr/status preservation. Tests were inspected, not executed, as required by this role.

The shared run() runner now validates a positive finite deadline and uses communicate(timeout=timeout), defaulting to COMMAND_TIMEOUT=120.0. Timeout cleanup calls stop_tree(), then communicates with REAP_TIMEOUT=5.0; the fallback wait and final launcher reap also have that bound. POSIX children start a new session and the process group is killed even when the direct child has already exited. Windows children launch behind a stdin token handshake, are assigned to a kill-on-close Job before receiving the token, and closing that Job terminates descendants. Direct children are reaped and streams are closed. UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT retains command, cwd, deadline, exit status, stdout and stderr. Existing Git fixtures and real pinned smoke therefore inherit hard subprocess deadlines. ProcessDeadlineTest covers a real timeout and two deterministic descendant scenarios, including the direct child already having exited. The descendant signals readiness after taking a file lock; queue.get, reader.join and parent.wait all use explicit five-second bounds. Injecting TimeoutExpired after readiness avoids relying on startup speed. Successful EOF, released nonblocking file lock and direct-child returncode establish tree termination and reaping. The deliberately blocking child Event.wait and readiness reader.readline are confined to killable children or a daemon reader with a bounded supervising queue/join. No sleeps, retries or timeout widening mask the original issue.
